sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Narendra Gupta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Shri Narendra Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Ankit Singh, brief holder of learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
3.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No.398 of 2018, under Sections 376-D, 506, 120-B I.P.C., Police Station Biswan, District Sitapur.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that Smt. Arti, wife of co-accused Deepu who is daughter-in-law of the applicant lodged FIR on 11.08.2018 in pursuance of the direction given by the court under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.
The said FIR was lodged against Rohit and Monu.
It is submitted that out of retaliation, the applicant has been implicated and his two sons co-accused have been implicated.
FIR has been lodged by Punam, wife of Durgesh on 11.10.2018 in pursuance of the application dated 25.08.2018 filed under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C.

Learned counsel submitted that the present case has been filed in retaliation of case crime no. 322 of 2018 under sections 452,
376D IPC at Police Station Biswan, District Sitapur lodged by daughter-in-law of the applicant (wife Indal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home, Lko. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45072497/
1 of co-accused) on 11.08.2018 which was registered against brother of the complainant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel further submitted that the medical report of the prosecutrix does not support the prosecution case and as per the doctor's report, there is no sign of use of force and no forceful penetration injury is found.
Learned counsel submitted that FIR has been lodged by the the prosecutrix against two sons of present applicant and father.
He submitted that in medical examination the prosecutrix has levelled allegation of rape against Ranjit and Deepu and no allegation of rape has been levelled against the applicant.

It is further submitted that the present FIR was challenged in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition N0.31799 of 2018 in which arrest stay of the applicant along with his sons was stayed and thereafter charge sheet was filed.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition N0.31799 of 2018
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 10.08.2023.

6. On the other hand, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. goes to indicate that allegation of rape is levelled against the applicant and co-accused therefore, bail is liable to be rejected.

7. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, after hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the argument that medical report does not support the prosecution case,
argument that present case has been filed in retaliation of Case Crime No.322 of 2018 and argument that applicant and his two sons have been falsely implicated, I find it to be a fit case for bail.

8. Let the applicant, Indal, be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to Indal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home, Lko.

The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
